key_insight: A deep neural operator can learn the mapping from problem inputs to both the PDE solution and its evolving free boundary, achieving high accuracy and real-time inference. This makes fast, generalizable simulation of moving-boundary phenomena (e.g., tumor growth) feasible for clinical use.
problem_solved: Computational and modeling difficulty of free boundary problems: traditional PDE solvers are expensive and hard to generalize across varying conditions, limiting real‑time and patient‑specific simulations needed in clinical settings.
method: Develop a neural operator framework that directly approximates the solution operator for PDEs with free (moving) boundaries, outputting full spatio-temporal fields and boundary evolution.
Train the operator on high-fidelity examples so it generalizes across initial conditions and parameters, replacing costly iterative solvers at inference time.
Architectural and training choices prioritize precision and low-latency inference to enable real-time predictions for downstream applications.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable surrogate modeling approach for complex, moving-boundary physics—enabling fast, generalizable simulations and potential integration into clinical decision-support tools like tumor-growth forecasting.
visual_elements: Schematic of a free boundary: sequence of frames showing domain evolution (e.g., tumor boundary over time) to convey the moving-boundary problem.
Block diagram of the neural operator mapping inputs (initial state, parameters) to solution field + boundary output to explain the model role.
Comparison chart: accuracy vs runtime for neural operator vs conventional PDE solvers to highlight precision and speedup.
Application graphic: stylized clinical workflow showing real-time simulation used for patient-specific planning/monitoring.
paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
paper_authors: Zongjia Long, Qi Zhou, Aiqing Zhu, Dong Dai, Yiqun Liu
